e0d7ea803158c275a7346347fb1e02b3f18be34e.summary: A Trend Micro TrendLabs blog post, published 2013-02-27, describes the remote access trojan BKDR_RARSTONE.A. It was found in a spear phishing email carrying a .DOC file. Like PlugX, it loads a backdoor directly into memory without dropping a file, and it injects code into a hidden Internet Explorer process. It communicates over SSL and can enumerate, transfer and execute files. It can also silently uninstall applications such as anti-malware software. Trend Micro says its products detect and block it and that it will monitor the trojan and investigate any campaigns behind it.

It credits Malpedia, Cisco Talos and CERT-Orange CyberDefense as sources and shows commit and archive metadata. It gives no threat analysis of its own, so it is an index rather than a threat report.

e012644ba7c04c8fc85518ff6ffb20e4bef11b93.summary: Sekoia's threat intelligence team investigated the Quad7 (7777) botnet, which uses compromised, mostly TP-Link routers to relay password spraying against Microsoft 365 accounts. They monitored one router and recovered malware from a victim router in France: a Socks5 proxy and a bind shell named xlogin. The report links the activity to likely business email compromise by cybercriminals rather than an APT, but leaves attribution, the exploited vulnerabilities and the geographic distribution unresolved.
